title: Inspect typed DNS routing and metadata records
goal: Inspect non-SRV DNS address, mail, text, alias, reverse-name and name-server records with TTLs, distinct negative results and explicit resolver selection.

selectionNotes: Explicit Windows DNS servers require one address family and port 0/53; Linux supports custom ports. Negative TTL is best-effort and can be zero on Windows. No service selection or peer authentication.

sdk.reason: Build against .NET 11 references; exact RC2 pin records verification.

language.reason: Declared canonical language mode; no preview syntax required.
language.name: C#

packageAssets: Framework reference/runtime assemblies; no primary-route NuGet package.
providers: Windows DNSAPI/DnsQueryEx; Linux managed DNS wire resolver and framework sockets with normal runtime native dependencies.
platforms: Windows x64 DnsQueryEx/DNSAPI and Linux x64 managed resolver/socket route executed. macOS source-reviewed only; browser/mobile/WASI excluded.
prerequisites: Console net11.0 project, C# 15.0, nullable and implicit usings; exact RC2 versions are tested baselines.
Trusted DNS endpoint and working sockets; local proof needs free loopback UDP 53 on Windows or isolated Linux ephemeral ports. No public-zone dependency.

sources.title: DNS negative caching and SOA lifetimes

evidence.scope: Real Windows authoritative UDP records/TTLs, NODATA/NXDOMAIN/SOA absence, server override and pre/in-flight cancellation. Current Windows negative TTL is zero; separate Linux evidence measures positive TTL.

Actual network-none Linux x64 authoritative UDP records, exact fields/TTLs, negative SOA TTL 45 versus absent SOA zero, two custom-port server overrides, pre/in-flight cancellation and removed container.
